brief.title: The 10-minute idea rescue
brief.premise: A rough idea becomes usable when the creator names one audience and one takeaway.
brief.audience: Solo creators staring at a half-written note
brief.creativeGoal: Help the viewer turn one vague note into a filmable short
brief.desiredTakeaway: Clarity comes from narrowing the idea, not waiting for inspiration.
brief.spokenHook: Your idea probably is not bad. It is just carrying too many jobs.
brief.firstFrameText: Rescue a rough idea in 10 minutes

scriptBeats.label: Name the friction
scriptBeats.script: When a note feels impossible to film, it usually has more than one audience or takeaway hiding inside it.

scriptBeats.label: Show the move
scriptBeats.script: Circle the one person this is for, then finish this sentence: after watching, I want them to believe or do this one thing.

brief.close: That is enough structure to make the next creative decision.
brief.ctaIntent: Invite the viewer to try the narrowing prompt on a saved idea.

filmingGuidance.setup: Direct-to-camera at a desk with the original note visible.
filmingGuidance.delivery: Calm and matter-of-fact, with a pause before the narrowing prompt.
filmingGuidance.editing: Use two clean cuts and hold the prompt long enough to read.
filmingGuidance.audio: Prioritize clear voice; optional low instrumental bed.

proposedTasks.title: Record the desk walkthrough
proposedTasks.notes: Capture the note close-up immediately after the talking-head take.

assumptions: The creator is comfortable appearing on camera.

platformVariants.caption: One audience. One takeaway. That is enough to rescue the note.

platformVariants.openingAdjustment: Show the messy note before the first spoken word.
editChanges: Start with the note close-up for half a second.

platformVariants.title: How to Rescue a Rough Video Idea
